Tested OpenRouter tencent/hy3:free on two rollout prompt groups with all six generations included per group, and opencode-go mimo-v2.5 on two direct generation prompts; recorded speed, parseability, and local quality checks without persisting API keys.

Tightened teacher_scoring.py prompt into a validation-first rubric with hard-failure rules and score caps for format/schema/range/count/arithmetic/gold-answer violations.

Fixed teacher_scoring.py head-of-line blocking by replacing fixed-size batch waits with a sliding-window executor; completed worker slots now immediately receive new prompt groups while stragglers continue in background slots.
Retried failed mimo-v2.5 teacher labels, exported q>=8 teacher-clean SFT candidates, and created stricter parse/schema-valid SFT candidate files with quarantine manifests.

Converted SFT model and base model to Q4_K_M GGUF format, ran inference evaluations on all 153 prompts, and evaluated math reasoning on 100 GSM8K prompts. Results show a major formatting improvement (JSON validity +76.5%, factual QA accuracy +17.6%) but a 15% regression in GSM8K (54% vs 69% base) due to task drift/catastrophic forgetting.

Refreshed the lenovo HY3 seven-family agentic trajectory export after targeted state-compaction recovery and exporter hygiene fixes. The strict SFT export now has every requested family above 100 clean prompt-matched traces, while collection continues toward the full 7,000-instance x 4-8 rollout target.

Started a capped HY3 balanced-shard supervisor on lenovo and refreshed strict SFT/DPO exports. The supervisor keeps collection moving by launching the next incomplete balanced shard only when active HY3 shard workers drop below six.
Refreshed HY3 agentic trajectory exports at the 1,000-clean-trace checkpoint and generated deterministic stratified SFT/DPO train-validation splits for first-pass training while collection continues.
Added and started a periodic HY3 export refresher on lenovo so clean SFT, DPO, and stratified training-ready split files update automatically while capped HY3 collection continues.

Cleaned HY3 training-ready chat fields: SFT assistant trajectories no longer duplicate the leading user turn, and DPO rows now include `chosen_messages` and `rejected_messages` for direct preference training consumers.

Added tiered HY3 DPO split files separating explicit hard-negative preference pairs from successful-but-less-efficient rollout contrasts, then refreshed training-ready exports while collection continued.

Sanitized trainable HY3 trajectory transcript exports to remove repository-internal/cache path noise from tool calls, tool results, terminal commands, and assistant text while preserving raw Hermes traces for audit; refreshed clean SFT, DPO, hard-negative DPO, and efficiency DPO splits while six HY3 workers continue collecting.

Recovered HY3 trajectory collection from wedged shard workers by adding process-group timeout termination and incomplete-run cleanup to the Hermes task runner, then restarted collection under a seven-worker supervisor without fresh rate-limit artifacts.

Trained LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct on a mixed dataset (413 formatting, 2,000 Magicoder, 1,600 GSM8K examples) for 300 steps, converted to GGUF format, and evaluated on formatting prompts and GSM8K. The mixed run failed to preserve math reasoning (GSM8K accuracy dropped to 48.0%) and failed formatting alignment (JSON validity 11.8%) under low-epoch constraints (1.2 epochs).

Exported intermediate checkpoint-200 (~3.9 epochs formatting SFT) to GGUF format and evaluated formatting prompts and GSM8K. Found that step-200 achieves a very strong balance: 76.5% GameFAQ JSON validity (close to step-300's 82.4%) while preserving higher math reasoning accuracy (56.0% vs step-300's 54.0%).

Merged step-200 adapter at scale 0.3 to GGUF format and evaluated on formatting and GSM8K. Found that scale 0.3 is below the activation threshold: formatting validity is low (11.8% JSON validity) but math reasoning is highly preserved (67.0% vs base 69.0%).

Merged step-200 adapter at scale 0.7 to GGUF format and evaluated on formatting and GSM8K. Found a highly robust trade-off point: 52.9% GameFAQ JSON validity and 88.2% structured JSON validity while preserving math reasoning at 60.0% (retaining 87% of base capacity).
Trained LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct on the cleaned 7.4k-row GSM8K dataset (stripping all out-of-distribution calculator annotations) to resolve syntax/repetition collapse; saved clean math adapter.

Directly merged Math adapter (weight 1.0) and Formatting adapter (checkpoint-200, weight 0.7) on the base LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct model by adding scaled delta weights in PyTorch, exported to GGUF format, and evaluated on formatting and GSM8K. Achieved 69.0% GSM8K accuracy (100% of base model math capability) while retaining 82.4% JSON validity.
